definitions.explanation: A military encampment or the arrangement of troops on a field. Survives mainly in set phrases and historical writing, and in figures of speech drawn from them.

definitions.gloss: corps; lineup; body of people (as a suffix)
definitions.explanation: As a suffix on a noun, the assembled group of people in one role: {報道陣|ほうどうじん} (the press corps), {首脳陣|しゅのうじん} (the top brass). This is by far the commoner use in modern Japanese.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{陣|じん}を{崩|くず}すのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Breaking the enemy's formation is difficult.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}を{背|せ}にして{陣|じん}を{構|かま}えたのは、{退|しりぞ}く{気|き}がなかったからだ。
examples.english: He took up position with the river at his back because he had no intention of retreating.

examples.japanese: {報道|ほうどう}{陣|じん}が{集|あつ}まった。
{今年|ことし}は{投手|とうしゅ}{陣|じん}が{厚|あつ}い。
examples.english: The pitching staff is deep this year.

examples.japanese: {首脳|しゅのう}{陣|じん}が{総入|そうい}れ{替|か}えになり、{会社|かいしゃ}の{方針|ほうしん}も{大|おお}きく{変|か}わった。
examples.english: The entire senior leadership was replaced, and the company's direction changed sharply.

notes:
Sense 2 is a suffix and never stands alone; learners meet it far more often than sense 1.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {報道|ほうどう}{陣|じん}: the press corps
- {首脳|しゅのう}{陣|じん}: the top leadership
- {投手|とうしゅ}{陣|じん}: the pitching staff
- {経営|けいえい}{陣|じん}: the management team

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {陣|じん}を{張|は}る: to encamp; to take up a position
- {背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}: a last stand with no way back
